subject: Morning Analyst Inbox — 2026-10-22
body:
# Morning Analyst Inbox — 2026-10-22

Focus today: META’s post-print model reset; NOK’s growth-versus-cash trade-off; LRCX’s shipment delays; WDC into tonight’s results; NVDA’s deployment economics.

Book prioritization is provisional: the portfolio remains a July 1 seed with unknown weights. Bloomberg’s snapshot is dated October 21, not a fully refreshed post-results consensus. Evidence key E: [today’s source checks](<E:/Wiki Felipe empresas/_wiki/_meta/analyst-evidence/2026-10-22-morning-source-checks.json>). “supp-” IDs are the saved research overlay, not generated alerts.

## Five priorities

1. META — better revenue visibility does not yet mean better earnings or funding clarity.

Hard evidence: Meta’s October 21 release reports Q3 revenue of $64.60bn and Q4 guidance of $73–76bn. It gives no numerical 2027 spending outlook. [Company release](https://investor.atmeta.com/investor-news/press-release-details/2026/Meta-Reports-Third-Quarter-2026-Results/default.aspx).

Broker revision: BofA/Post–Bansal, October 22, raises 2027 revenue to $319bn but cuts EPS by $0.24 to $34.00; its PT rises $810→$845 on a higher multiple. JPM/Anmuth, October 22, relays management’s early Muse engagement figures—10 million sign-ups and 25% daily usage—and models 2027 capex of $255bn. These are user-engagement claims and a broker forecast, not proven Muse profitability or company capex guidance.

Inference/action: prioritize the recurring-cost, depreciation and rented-capacity bridge before raising the valuation multiple. Separate advertising monetization already evidenced from agent economics still to be demonstrated. Falsifier of the cautious view: incremental AI revenue produces durable earnings/cash upside after infrastructure and funding costs.

ID: supp-20261022-meta-reset. Evidence: E; _wiki/META.md, Debate/Changelog; _wiki/_meta/reconciliation-2026-10-21-inbox.md.

2. NOK — the growth upgrade is real; cash conversion deteriorated.

Hard evidence: Nokia/Justin Hotard, October 22, reports 11.7% comparable operating margin and expects combined Optical/IP growth of 25–30% in 2027. But Mobile Infrastructure benefited from revenue accelerated from Q4, while FY26 free-cash-flow conversion falls to 35–55%, with an additional €400m working-capital investment. Full-year operating-profit guidance is unchanged. [Company release, pp.1–2](https://www.nokia.com/system/files/2026-10/nokia_results_2026_q3.pdf).

Source conflict resolved: MS/Terence Tsui’s October 22 email says 20–25% growth in its summary but 25–30% in its detail. The company PDF confirms 25–30%.

Inference/action: at today’s call, ask how much of the margin beat reverses in Q4, when inventory becomes cash, and how the optical manufacturing ramp supports the growth outlook. Do not annualize the quarter’s margin. Falsifier of the constructive growth case: ramp delays or weak backlog conversion persist while cash consumption rises.

IDs: cata-3e8cb5a41612; supp-20261022-nok-cash. Evidence: E; _wiki/NOK.md; company PDF archived in _wiki/_meta/analyst-evidence/.

3. LRCX — demand remains strong, but delayed shipments must actually catch up.

Hard evidence: Lam’s October 21 release reports revenue of $8.22bn and non-GAAP EPS of $2.20; December guidance is $8.60bn ± $400m and EPS $2.33 ± $0.15. [Company release](https://investor.lamresearch.com/2026-10-21-Lam-Research-Corporation-Reports-Financial-Results-for-the-Quarter-Ended-September-27%2C-2026).

Broker evidence: JPM/Harlan Sur, October 22, says guidance missed buy-side expectations and relays management’s expectation that supply-delayed shipments move into March, alongside a preliminary CY27 WFE outlook above $200bn. Susquehanna/Mehdi Hosseini, October 22, also flags component shortages and supplier price increases.

Inference/action: investigate whether equipment suppliers can convert demand into shipments without surrendering margin to component vendors. Separate China’s sequential decline from supply-related delays. Falsifier of the timing-only bull case: March catch-up slips, orders weaken, or component inflation erodes margins.

ID: supp-20261022-lrcx-supply. Evidence: E; _wiki/LRCX.md; canonical comparison in _wiki/_meta/assumptions.md, wfe-tam. The company’s new WFE outlook is a distinct source vintage, not an automatic house-model revision.

4. WDC — tonight’s test is the investor bar, not a target-price increase.

Evidence: BofA/Wamsi Mohan, October 21, raises PT $720→$800 but expects December EPS guidance of $5.00 ± $0.15. MS/Erik Woodring, October 20, models $5.25 and reports buy-side expectations of $5.20–$5.60.

Inference/action: a consensus beat could still disappoint investors. Prepare a price/volume/product-transition bridge and ask whether supply discipline survives the next capacity ramp. This is an unchanged thesis with a newly immediate catalyst, not fresh bullish evidence. Falsifier of the cautious trading setup: guidance clears investor expectations with credible shipment execution.

ID: supp-20261022-wdc-bogey. Evidence: E; _wiki/WDC.md; _wiki/_meta/analyst-evidence/2026-10-20-morning-source-checks.json and 2026-10-21-morning-source-checks.json.

5. NVDA — faster commissioning could improve customer cash flow, but it is not a financing cure.

Hard evidence: NVIDIA’s October 21 DSX POD announcement targets early-2027 availability and deployment from six months to as little as 14 days at a prepared site. Its separate supply-chain release announces a $1.1bn KYEC capacity-reservation advance supporting US testing facilities, with high-volume production targeted for April 2027. These are company plans; neither proves completed facilities or customer cash savings. [DSX POD](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-introduces-dsx-pod-ai-factories-to-accelerate-europes-infrastructure-deployment); [supplier commitments](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-and-supply-chain-partners-expand-capacity-to-accelerate-ai-infrastructure-buildout).

Inference/action: MS/Joseph Moore, October 22, sees faster bring-up as a neocloud cash-flow advantage. Test that against actual site-readiness, acceptance and billing dates. The prepared-site condition leaves power and permitting risk intact. Falsifier: factory integration improves but grid readiness or customer funding still delays paid utilization.

ID: supp-20261022-nvda-deployment. Evidence: E; _wiki/NVDA.md; _wiki/themes/ai-compute-deals.md, NVDA-KYEC-TEST-20261021. Supplier reservations are not additional compute TCV or delivered MW.

## Model adjudication and sentiment

- META: Capstone’s October 12 model carries FY26 capex of $150.7bn versus company guidance of $135–145bn, and expenses of $162bn versus $175–179bn including the $9.89bn legal charge. Bridge charge, recurring costs and capex basis before changing forecasts. For 2027, house capex of $200bn now faces JPM/Anmuth’s October 22 $255bn. ID supp-20261022-meta-reset; E; reconciliation and _wiki/_data/house.json.
- Funding timing is disputed even within JPM: Schilsky’s October 21 first take, circulated October 22, suggests Class C points toward a 2027 raise; Anmuth’s October 22 note says a raise can occur before January. No offering timetable was announced. Do not turn either interpretation into a financing milestone. Same ID/evidence.
- Carryover controls: GOOG house June 5 revenue remains $505bn/$641bn for 2026/27 versus Bloomberg October 21 $430.5bn/$547.9bn; reconcile period and recognition basis first. IDs esti-5a79fad25b6e / esti-de85d0b82ebe. CRWV’s −$3.27 house EPS, October 14, is a smaller loss than Bloomberg October 21’s −$3.91—not “below” as the engine labels it. ID esti-d865f3088118. Evidence: E; _wiki/_data/house.json and estimates.json.
- Sentiment interpretation: monetization optimism is improving faster than funding confidence. JPM Market Intelligence/Ellen Wang, October 22, reports META reversing its initial after-hours gain to approximately −2% premarket amid broader technology/geopolitical risk-off. This is a dated desk observation, not a live quote or proof that the results caused the decline. ID supp-20261022-meta-reset; E.

## Catalysts and preparation

- Today, NOK: webcast at 3 p.m. Finnish time/EEST. Prioritize pull-forward, working capital and manufacturing-ramp questions above. IDs cata-3e8cb5a41612 / supp-20261022-nok-cash; E. [Company October 15 notice](https://www.nokia.com/newsroom/nokia-to-publish-third-quarter-and-january-september-2026-interim-report-on-22-october-2026/).
- Today, WDC: after close; call 4:30 p.m. ET. Freeze the investor EPS bar before the release. ID supp-20261022-wdc-bogey; E. [Company October 8 notice](https://www.westerndigital.com/en-in/company/newsroom/press-releases/2026/2026-10-08-wd-to-announce-first-quarter-fiscal-year-2027-financial-results).
- Today, GTC’s final day: collect customer acceptance/production commitments, not only design announcements. Do not treat the entire event as already resolved. ID supp-20261022-nvda-deployment; E; JPM Market Intelligence calendar, October 22.

## What materially changed versus yesterday

META has reported, broker revenue/EPS revisions now diverge, and Muse engagement evidence is richer than yesterday’s release-only coverage. NOK moves from a technical AI-RAN milestone to a quantified growth outlook with weaker cash conversion. LRCX adds a concrete supply-constrained guide and March catch-up test. GTC adds supplier commitments and a prepared-site deployment proposition. WDC’s expectations are carried forward unchanged; the print is now today.

Engine October 22: 47 active alerts, five high, zero belief-change flags. Yesterday’s published morning brief had 48/five; its later saved daily snapshot had 51/seven. Against that later snapshot, META/MU calendar entries and two belief flags disappear, with no new IDs. This is not evidence that all underlying debates resolved.

The premature GTC postmortem (post-8cd5d82dc530), future-dated closed NVDA fireside and stale reconciliation extraction remain quality exceptions. Today’s October 21 reconciliation was reviewed manually. Evidence: E; _wiki/_data/analyst/history/signals-2026-10-21.json and signals-2026-10-22.json.

No company pages or house models were edited. Evidence/history, narrow outcome assessments, the supplier-capacity timeline and derived views were updated.
